title: Returning Result from Tests
goal: Learn how tests can return Result<(), E> to use the ? operator.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Morning: Unit Tests

sections.text: Unit tests do not have to return `()`. They can also return `Result<(), E>` where `E` implements `std::fmt::Debug`.

sections.caption: Use ? inside tests to fail automatically on Err.

sections.text: Returning `Result` lets you use the `?` operator directly in test functions. If an operation evaluates to `Err`, `?` exits early and `cargo test` reports the failure.
A test that returns `Result` must explicitly return `Ok(())` as its final value. Returning a value inside `Ok` like `Ok(42)` is a compiler error because test runners expect unit `()`.

explanation: Learn how tests can return Result<(), E> to use the ? operator.
